meta.title: Shall We Study Together?
meta.textType: story: a study lunch with suggestions, and a feeling that the text does not state

paragraphs: On Tuesday, March second, Lily, Mia, Leo, and May had their first study lunch. They sat at a big table in the school library at half past twelve. The room was quiet, and a few other pupils read at the far tables. Each of them had a notebook, and the science test was next Wednesday. "Shall we read our notes first?" asked May. "Let's make a quiz game instead!" said Leo. "The library closes at one o'clock," said May. "We have only a short time, so let's start with the notes." She opened her notebook and pointed at the first page.

Leo said nothing for a moment. Then he put the books in a pile with a loud bump. He took his pencil and drew a small paw print on his page. "OK, notes first," he said in a flat voice. "The test has two parts," said May. "Teacher Kim told us in class," she added. "Teacher Kim says that salt and water make a mixture," said Mia. "How can we work out the answer to question two?" asked May. Mia worked it out easily and wrote it in her notebook. May wrote it down as well. Lily noticed that Leo's page was still empty. Mia looked at the clock. "Shall we try one round of Leo's quiz at the end?" she asked. "Good idea," said May. "Let's start it at ten to one." Leo's pencil stopped.

At ten to one, the four children leaned over one open page. Leo took a small card out of his bag, and the word "QUIZ" was on it. A sign on a shelf said, "The library closes at one o'clock." "Hey, here is question one!" said Leo with a big smile. "What do you get when you mix salt and water?"

"A mixture," said Mia. "That was easy." "Question two," said Leo, and he held up the card. "Can you get the salt back?" "Yes, if you heat the water," said Lily. Mia clapped her hands, and May laughed. "Mia and Lily have one point each," said Leo. "Everybody can get more points, and we can decide the winner later." "Let's play together, with no winner," said May.

At one o'clock, the children put their notes in their bags. "Anyway, I like your quiz, Leo," said May. "Maybe we can play it again on Friday," said Lily. "Can I bring the cards?" asked Leo. "Yes, please," said Mia. "Remember to bring your notes first," said May with a smile.
text.summary: The four friends have their first study lunch in the library before the science test. Leo wants a quiz game, but May wants to read the notes first, and at the end the quiz begins.
